ch1-006.does: Adds two numbers using R as a calculator.

ch1-008.does: Divides 5 by 3; R prints decimals to 7 significant digits by default.

ch1-009.does: Raises 5 to the power 3 with the ^ operator.

ch1-010.does: Evaluates the parentheses first, then multiplies.

ch1-011.does: Calls the function sqrt() on the input 4.

ch1-012.does: Assigns the value of 5 + 3 to a new object named result with <-; nothing is printed.

ch1-013.does: Typing an object's name prints its value (auto-printing).
ch1-013.out: The value currently stored in result.

ch1-014.does: Prints the object explicitly with print(); same display as auto-printing.
ch1-014.out: The value currently stored in result.

ch1-015.does: Reassigns result, overwriting its previous value with 5 - 3.

ch1-016.does: Prints result after it was overwritten.
ch1-016.out: The new value of result after reassignment.

ch1-017.does: Stores a character string (text in quotes) in an object named kosuke.

ch1-018.out: The stored character string, shown in quotes.

ch1-019.does: Overwrites kosuke with a longer string; spaces are allowed inside strings.

ch1-020.out: The new character string stored in kosuke.

ch1-021.does: Stores the number 5 as text (a character string) in Result, a different object from result because names are case-sensitive.

ch1-022.does: Prints Result; the quotes show it is character, not numeric.

ch1-023.does: Prints the lowercase object result, which is unaffected by Result.
ch1-023.out: The numeric value stored in result.

ch1-024.does: Asks for the class of result.

ch1-026.does: Asks for the class of Result.
ch1-026.out: The class of Result: character (a number stored as text).

ch1-027.does: Asks for the class of sqrt, showing functions are objects too.

ch1-028.does: Creates a numeric vector of world population estimates with c() (concatenate).

ch1-029.does: Prints the vector; [1] marks that the first printed element is element 1.
ch1-029.out: All seven world population estimates (in thousands).

ch1-030.does: Creates a vector of the first three population estimates.

ch1-031.does: Creates a vector of the last four population estimates.

ch1-032.does: Combines two vectors into one with c(); order is preserved.

ch1-033.out: All seven estimates, identical to world.pop.

ch1-034.does: Extracts the 2nd element with square-bracket indexing.

ch1-035.does: Extracts elements 2 and 4 by indexing with a vector of positions.
ch1-035.out: The 2nd and 4th estimates, in that order.

ch1-036.does: Extracts elements 4 and 2; the order of indices controls the order of output.

ch1-037.does: A negative index drops that element; the original vector is unchanged.

ch1-038.does: Divides every element by 1000 (vectorized arithmetic) to convert thousands to millions.

ch1-039.does: Prints the rescaled vector; [7] on the second line marks the 7th element.
ch1-039.out: World population in millions for each decade.

ch1-040.does: Divides every element by the first element, expressing each estimate relative to 1950.

ch1-041.out: Each decade's population as a multiple of the 1950 population (1950 = 1).

ch1-042.does: Subtracts the vector without its last element from the vector without its first element, giving each decade's increase.

ch1-043.does: Divides each increase by the starting population of that decade and multiplies by 100.

ch1-044.out: Percentage population increase for each decade (1950s through 2000s).

ch1-045.does: Replaces the first two elements with new values by assigning to those indices.

ch1-046.out: Percentage increases with the first two replaced by rounded values.

ch1-047.does: Counts the elements of the vector.
ch1-047.out: The number of elements in world.pop.

ch1-050.does: Returns the minimum and maximum together.
ch1-050.out: The range: smallest and largest estimates.

ch1-052.does: Computes the mean by hand: sum divided by number of elements.
ch1-052.out: The mean population estimate (same as mean()).

ch1-053.does: Creates a sequence from 1950 to 2010 in steps of 10 using named arguments of seq().

ch1-055.does: Same seq() call with arguments reordered; naming arguments makes order irrelevant.

ch1-056.does: A negative by value creates a decreasing sequence.

ch1-057.does: The colon operator creates an integer sequence increasing by 1.

ch1-058.does: The colon operator counting down by 1.

ch1-059.does: Asks for the names attribute of the vector.
ch1-059.out: NULL: the vector has no names yet.

ch1-060.does: Assigns the year vector as element names of world.pop.

ch1-061.does: Asks for the names attribute again.
ch1-061.out: The years, stored as character labels.

ch1-062.does: Prints the named vector; each value appears under its label.

ch1-063.does: Defines a user-written function my.summary() that returns a named vector of the sum, length, and mean of its input.

ch1-065.does: Applies the user-defined function to z.
ch1-065.out: The sum, length, and mean of the integers 1 to 10, labeled.

ch1-066.does: Applies the same function to world.pop.
ch1-066.out: The sum, length, and mean of the population estimates, labeled.

ch1-067.does: Loads a CSV file from the working directory into a data frame named UNpop.

ch1-068.does: Asks for the class of the loaded object.

ch1-069.does: Loads the objects saved in an RData file; no assignment needed because objects keep their saved names.

ch1-070.does: Lists the variable (column) names of the data frame.

ch1-071.out: The number of rows in UNpop.

ch1-072.out: The number of columns in UNpop.

ch1-074.does: Summarizes each variable with min, quartiles, median, mean, and max.
ch1-074.out: Five-number summaries plus the mean for year and world.pop.

ch1-075.does: Extracts one variable from the data frame with the $ operator, returning a vector.
ch1-075.out: The world.pop column as a vector.

ch1-076.does: Extracts a column by name with [ , "name"] indexing (all rows).
ch1-076.out: The world.pop column as a vector.

ch1-077.does: Extracts rows 1 to 3 and all columns (blank column index).
ch1-077.out: The first three rows of UNpop, both columns.

ch1-078.does: Extracts rows 1 to 3 of the year column.

ch1-079.does: Indexes a variable with a sequence 1, 3, 5, ... up to the number of rows.

ch1-080.does: Appends a missing value NA to the end of the population vector.

ch1-081.does: Prints the vector with its missing value.
ch1-081.out: The seven estimates followed by NA.

ch1-082.does: Takes the mean of a vector containing NA.
ch1-082.out: NA: mean() returns missing when any value is missing.

ch1-083.does: Takes the mean after removing missing values with na.rm = TRUE.
ch1-083.out: The mean of the seven non-missing estimates.
